title: An optimized protocol for PD-L1 pathological assessment with patient sample deglycosylation to improve correlation with therapeutic response
protocol: Place the slides on a staining rack in a 40°C oven overnight (12–18 h).
Bake the slides in a dry oven at 58°C–65°C for 2–3 h the next day (day 2).
Cool the slides to room temperature before proceeding to the next step.
Deparaffinize or dewax slides in xylene solution for 10 min in each container, 6 times.
Rehydrate the slides by sequentially dipping them into a series of ethanol baths: 10 dips per container, 3 times.
Dip slides 10 times each into containers of 95% ethanol, repeating this process three times.
Rinse slides three times with distilled water.
Substitute xylene with Histo-clear solution for less toxicity and better environmental friendliness.
Immerse slides in citrate buffer at 10 mM pH 6.0.
Heat the slides in a microwave oven at 1,000 W for 2 minutes followed by 200 W for 8 minutes.
Allow the slides to cool down naturally for 1-2 hours to room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash the slides twice with PBS for 5 minutes each.
Discard the PBS.
Fill the staining jar with glycoprotein denaturing buffer to cover the slides.
Incubate the slides at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 3 hours.
Immerse slides in glycoprotein denaturing buffer at room temperature for up to 3 hours.
Wash the slides with PBS for 5 minutes, repeating four times.
Immerse the slides with PBS.
Proceed with the PNGase F treatment procedure immediately.
Remove a maximum of 4–6 slides per 2–3 patients from the container at one time.
Drain and shake off the excess PBS.
Carefully wipe around the specimen on each slide.
Create a hydrophobic barrier around the slide specimen with a PAP pen.
Add enough appropriate solution to cover specimens processed with or without deglycosylation.
With deglycosylation: add 5% PNGase F solution to the specimen on the slide labeled with “+”.
Without deglycosylation: add PBS solvent alone to the specimen on the slide labeled with “−”.
Apply the average volume of 200 μL per section on a slide for tissue sections.
Place slides flat with the specimen facing upward in a humid chamber.
Place the humid chamber in a 37°C incubator in air supplemented with 5% CO2 for 12–18 h.
Remove the humid chamber with slides from the incubator and place it on a bench the next day (day 3).
Drain and shake off excess solution from the slides.
Place the slides in a clean staining jar filled with PBS.
Wash the slides with PBS for 5 min, 2 times.
After sample deglycosylation has completed, process tissue sections using a routinely used conventional IHC method.
Incubate the slides with 3% hydrogen peroxide solution for 10 minutes in a humid chamber at room temperature.
Wash the slides with PBS for 5 minutes, repeating this step three times.
Incubate the slides with 10% blocking buffer (normal goat serum in PBS) for 30 minutes in a humid chamber at room temperature.
Wipe off excess blocking buffer from the slides.
Prepare a 1:100 dilution of anti-PD-L1 rabbit monoclonal antibody in PBS.
Apply the diluted primary antibody to the tissue sections on the slides.
Incubate the slides in a humid chamber at 4°C overnight (12–18 hours).
Wash the slides with PBS for 5 minutes, repeating 3 times (day 4).
Incubate tissue sections overnight at 4°C with a 1:100 dilution of anti-PD-L1 antibody in PBS (10 μg/mL).
Prepare a 1:200 dilution of biotin-conjugated secondary antibody in PBS.
Apply the diluted secondary antibody to the tissue sections on the slides.
Incubate the slides in a humid chamber for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash the slides with PBS for 5 minutes, repeating three times.
Prepare a 1:100 dilution of ABC-HRP conjugate in PBS.
Apply the diluted ABC-HRP conjugate to the tissue sections on the slides.
Incubate the slides in a humid chamber for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Wash the slides with PBS for 5 minutes, repeating three times.
Prepare fresh AEC chromogen substrate working solution at a concentration of 0.125%.
Incubate the slides in a staining dish filled with the working solution for 5 to 10 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Rinse the slides with distilled water, repeating three times.
Incubate the slides in Mayer’s hematoxylin for 20 to 30 seconds.
Rinse the slides with distilled water, repeating three times.
Apply aqueous mounting medium to the tissue sections on the slides.
Place a coverslip on top of each slide.
Lay the slides flat to dry prior to viewing them under a microscope.
